:::{#cor-chain-qf}

#### Vector chain rule for quadratic forms

If $\vlsresid = \vlsresid\sparen{\vcoef}$ is an $n \times 1$ vector-valued function
of the $p \times 1$ vector $\vcoef$,
with continuous partial derivatives, then

$$
\underbrace{\deriv{\vcoef}{\paren{\vlsresid\sparen{\vcoef}\cdot \vlsresid\sparen{\vcoef}}}}_{p \times 1}
= \underbrace{\paren{\deriv{\vcoef}\vlsresid\sparen{\vcoef}}}_{p \times n}
\underbrace{\paren{2 \vlsresid\sparen{\vcoef}}}_{n \times 1}
$$

:::

::: proof
Apply @thm-chain-vec with $\vx = \vcoef$, $\vy = \vlsresid$, $q = n$,
and $z = f(\vlsresid) = \vlsresid \cdot \vlsresid = \tp{\vlsresid}\vlsresid$:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vcoef}\paren{\vlsresid \cdot \vlsresid}
&= \paren{\deriv{\vcoef}\vlsresid} \deriv{\vlsresid}\paren{\dprod{\vlsresid}{\vlsresid}}
&& \text{(vector chain rule)}
\\
&= \paren{\deriv{\vcoef}\vlsresid} \paren{2\vlsresid}
&& \text{(derivative of a simple quadratic form, in } \vlsresid \text{)}
\ea
$$

The second step is @cor-deriv-normsq,
applied to the $n \times 1$ vector $\vlsresid$ in place of $\vcoef$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-chain-qf-residuals}
#### Derivative of the residual sum of squares

Let $\vy$ ($n \times 1$) and $\mX$ ($n \times p$) be constant with respect to $\vcoef$,
and let $\vlsresid(\vcoef) = \vy - \mX\vcoef$ be the residual vector (@def-residual).
By @thm-deriv-linear-map, $\deriv{\vcoef}(\mX\vcoef) = \tp{\mX}$,
and $\deriv{\vcoef}\vy = \matr{0}_{p \times n}$ because $\vy$ is constant,
so $\deriv{\vcoef}\vlsresid = -\tp{\mX}$ ($p \times n$).
By @cor-chain-qf:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vcoef}\paren{\vlsresid \cdot \vlsresid}
&= \paren{-\tp{\mX}} \paren{2\vlsresid}
&& \text{(vector chain rule for quadratic forms)}
\\
&= -2\,\tp{\mX}\paren{\vy - \mX\vcoef}
&& \text{(substitute } \vlsresid = \vy - \mX\vcoef \text{)}
\ea
$$

Setting this $p \times 1$ vector to $\vzero$ gives the normal equations
$\tp{\mX}\mX\vcoef = \tp{\mX}\vy$ of least squares.

:::
